authority.exception_to: owner ruling 286 (reasoning bytes are projected out at the transport on every path; policy hash-and-stats-only-v1)
authority.owner_rulings: owner rulings 329 A and 330 A (2026-10-18, the R2b READ section of docs/readiness/2026-09-16-slurp-next-stage-owner-decisions-v1.md)
authority.owner_words_english: Decision 329: A. Decision 330: A. (Decision 330 A: a bounded diagnostic exception to ruling 286 -- one small registered probe re-issues the sealed Solver requests of about 40 R2b rows, forced and natural, both budgets, with the reasoning bytes RETAINED under the data root only, to classify the non-terminating reasoning as enumeration or a repetition loop; 286 stays in force for every other cell.)

non_claims: A diagnostic of reasoning shape on TRAIN Fold B development rows. It claims no score, no benefit and no change to the lock.
question: Is the Solver reasoning that fails to terminate at the 3,072-token budget an ENUMERATION (the model verifies every supplied item and candidate intent once or twice, in supply order, with no stopping rule) or a REPETITION LOOP (a small block restated over and over)?

read.pairs: forced-both rows: the 3072 reasoning against the 6144 reasoning of the same row (common prefix up to the forced close, repeat onset offsets)

reissue.raised_arm_requests: RE-ISSUED (coordinator decision 2, ruling 330 A 'both budgets'): the solver-6144 requests of the 16 forced-both rows. The resident np4 server admits them (max_tokens is a request parameter; no -n cap in the server arguments). Retained as <sample>.b6144.txt.
reissue.reconstruction_proof: sha256 of the adapter's canonical serialisation of the sealed payload equals the sealed payload_sha256 and the first-visit request_sha256; verified offline for all 56 contacts by `solver_reasoning_diag.py verify` (and the exact wire body rendered by the transport's own renderer)
reissue.reproduction_caveat: np4 batching is not deterministic: the re-issued reasoning may differ from the sealed one; the hash match or mismatch is recorded per row.
reissue.what: the sealed Solver MODEL_REQUEST payload of each roster row's budget-3072 first-visit contact (40 contacts) and, for the forced-both rows, of the solver-6144 contact (16 contacts), rebuilt from the sealed trace and sent through the registered llama-server transport unchanged (decoding: temperature 0, seed 20260913, the sealed id_slot; thinking_budget_tokens 3072 / max_tokens 4096 for the first 40, 6144 / 7168 for the last 16)
reissue.workers: one sequential worker per sealed id_slot, so every sent payload is the sealed payload byte for byte; within a slot the budget-3072 requests come first and the budget-6144 requests after them

retention.hash_check: sha256 of the retained bytes versus the sealed reasoning_content_sha256: match or mismatch recorded per row (results.jsonl)
retention.mechanism: core.reasoning_knobs.ReasoningRetention, buildable only from a plan whose run id is the diagnostic run id and whose profile is bounded-discovery-probe; an explicit constructor argument of the transport, never a model-fragment key; the stored wire message, the envelope reasoning object and every trace record remain the decision-286 projection
retention.text_policy: reasoning text never enters a document, a note, a commit, a ledger row or a chat transcript; only counts and pattern statistics do

roster.selection_rule: per group the quota is split evenly over supplied bin (<40, >=40 items of the budget-3072 arm's Solver request) x empty gold; rank = sha256(seed|group|sample_id); a short stratum is backfilled from the group in the same rank order

stop_rules: the first failure stops every worker; nothing is retried
one attempt: an existing diagnostic directory refuses the launch
the call ceiling is a hard stop
a flight lock, a flight process or a resident session other than think-budget-np4 refuses the launch
